# References, glossary, and annotations {short-title="References"}

This chapter presents the bibliographic citation system (IEEE style via
`IEEEtran-francais.bst`), the glossary and acronym system, collaborative comments,
and special front matter pages.

## Bibliographic citations {#sec-citations}

### Basic syntax

Citations are inserted with `[@key]`. The key corresponds to the BibTeX identifier
defined in `references.bib`:

````markdown
Computer typesetting was revolutionised by Knuth [@Knuth1984],
whose \TeX{} system was made accessible by Lamport with \LaTeX{} [@Lamport1994].
Quarto [@Allaire2022] unifies these tools in a modern publishing environment.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:** 

Computer typesetting was revolutionised by Knuth
[@Knuth1984], whose \TeX{} system was made accessible by Lamport with \LaTeX{}
[@Lamport1994]. Quarto [@Allaire2022] unifies these tools in a modern publishing
environment.
:::

### Multiple references

````markdown
Python visualisation tools [@Hunter2007] and typographic reference works
[@Bringhurst2004; @Mittelbach2023] complement the author's toolkit.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:** 

Python visualisation tools [@Hunter2007] and typographic reference works
[@Bringhurst2004; @Mittelbach2023] complement the author's toolkit.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Always use `[@key]` with brackets

The `IEEEtran-francais.bst` style uses `natbib`. The `@key` syntax without brackets
calls `\citet{}` which is broken with IEEEtran — it produces the author name followed
by `[?]`. **Always use `[@key]`** to obtain `[N]` (IEEE numbering).
:::

### The `references.bib` file

The `references.bib` file must be located **at the project root**. Pandoc in natbib
mode generates `\bibliography{references}` (without a path), and BibTeX looks for the
file in the current directory. A file in `content_en/references.bib` will not be
found.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Bibliography managers

Zotero (with the Better BibTeX connector), JabRef, or Mendeley export directly to
`.bib` format. The `@IEEEtranBSTCTL` entry at the top of the file configures the
IEEEtran style (number of authors before "et al.", etc.) — do not remove it.
:::

## Glossary and acronyms {#sec-glossary}

### Declaring entries in `glossaire-entries.qmd`

All entries are declared in
`content_en/frontmatter/glossaire-entries.qmd` via two shortcodes:

````markdown
{{</* acr label ABBREV "Full expansion" */>}}
{{</* terme label "word" "Complete definition of the term" */>}}
````

The shortcodes automatically write `_glossaire-entries.tex` (read by LaTeX) and
populate the HTML tables. Labels must be unique.

### Using acronyms in the text

Four shortcodes allow referencing an acronym in the desired form:

| Shortcode | PDF output | HTML output |
|:----------|:-----------|:------------|
| `{{</* gls cnam */>}}` | short form (1st use: long) | short form |
| `{{</* acrs cnam */>}}` | always short form | always short form |
| `{{</* acrl cnam */>}}` | always long form | always long form |
| `{{</* acrf cnam */>}}` | long (short) | long (short) |

: Glossary reference shortcodes. {#tbl-gloss-shortcuts}

Examples in context:

````markdown
The {{</* acrs cnam */>}} ({{</* acrl cnam */>}}) was founded in 1794.
The {{</* acrf qmd */>}} format is Quarto's native format.
The {{< acrf toc >}} is generated automatically by Quarto.
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:** 

The {{< acrs cnam >}} ({{< acrl cnam >}}) was founded in 1794. The
{{< acrf qmd >}} format is Quarto's native format.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## PDF vs HTML behaviour

In PDF, `{{</* gls label */>}}` expands on the first occurrence (long form + abbreviation
in parentheses) then uses the short form. In HTML, this first-occurrence logic is not
handled by the shortcode — it always produces the short form. For consistency, prefer
`{{</* acrf label */>}}` on the first occurrence in the text, and `{{</* acrs label */>}}`
thereafter.
:::

## Collaborative comments (`quarto-comments`) {#sec-comments}

### Configuration in `_quarto.yml`

The `quarto-comments` extension (folder `_extensions/comments/`) is configured in
`_quarto.yml`, via the `quarto-comments:` key placed under the `extensions:` block {{< todo "You will need to walk me through your various YAML files at our next progress meeting." author="ag" >}}:

````yaml
extensions:
  quarto-comments:
    enabled: true
    authors:
      eb:
        name: "Eric Bavu"
      ag:
        name: "Abbé Grégoire"
      # Colors auto-assigned from Bootstrap 5 palette; override if needed:
      # nc:
      #   name: "Nicolas Conté"
      #   color_html: "#198754"
      #   color_latex: "green!30"
````

{{< pagebreak >}}


### The four comment types

````markdown
{{</* comment "Rephrase this sentence, it is too long." author="ag" */>}}
{{</* todo "Add a figure illustrating this point." author="eb" */>}}
{{</* note "See also Bringhurst 2004, §2.4." author="ag" */>}}
{{</* question "Is this result reproducible on another dataset?" author="ag" inline=true */>}}
````

**Rendered in context:**

Here is a sentence with a comment from the thesis supervisor (who added it directly in the {{< comment "This is a comment, to show that I too — Abbé Grégoire — am perfectly capable of editing a Quarto Markdown file myself!" author="ag" >}} `.qmd` file, because he is not shy about it!).

These comments are visible **only** if the `quarto-comments` option is set to `enabled: true` {{< todo "Remember to set this option to `false` before submitting to the reviewers!" author="eb" >}} in the `yaml` file — which is the case for this documentation.


It is also possible to add "long" inline comments {{< note "See Knuth 1984, chapter 12 — it would really be worth adding a discussion of this work here to show off all your knowledge of the existing literature, young apprentice." author="ag" inline=true >}} without taking up any space in the document margin. Useful to flesh out the text and add whole paragraphs. Note that, visually, the "inline" comment automatically breaks onto its own line and separates from the text in the PDF version, even when inserted mid-sentence.

::: {.callout-note}
## `inline=true` occupies the full line in PDF

In HTML, `inline=true` annotations appear as a compact coloured span, exactly
as wide as their content. In PDF, the `todonotes` package renders `\todo[inline]`
as a full-width coloured block — this is a design constraint of the package that
cannot be worked around without losing the ability to wrap long annotations across
lines.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Recommended: enable `wide_margins` for proofreading

For margin notes (without `inline`), it is **recommended to enable**
`extensions.quarto-comments.wide_margins: true` in your proofreading profile. The paper
is then widened outward by a dedicated strip (width adjustable via `extra_margin`) where
annotations display comfortably, with a grey background that alternates by page parity
(outer side, binding preserved).

When `wide_margins: false` (the default), the paper stays at standard A4 size: notes are
placed in the 2 cm outer margin. They therefore stay **narrow** (~1.5 cm) and long text
wraps over several lines. The **content** layout (text block) is strictly identical whether
`wide_margins` is `true` or `false`, and whether comments are enabled or not — only the
margin annotation zone changes.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Disable comments before final submission

Before submitting the thesis to the doctoral school and depositing it on theses.fr,
set `extensions.quarto-comments.enabled: false` in `_quarto.yml`. Annotations must not appear in the
official archived version.
:::

## Web annotations with Hypothesis (opt-in)

For remote proofreading, the HTML output can be enhanced with web annotations via
[Hypothesis](https://hypothes.is). Supervisors and reviewers select text in the browser
and add comments without touching the source files. Annotations are stored on Hypothesis
servers and tied to the page URL — they persist across renders as long as the URL stays
stable (GitHub Pages deployment recommended).

To enable, uncomment the following block in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format:
  cnam-thesis-html:
    comments:
      hypothesis:
        theme: clean   # clean = discreet ; classic = sidebar always visible
```

Then create a private group on [hypothes.is](https://hypothes.is) and share the invite
link with your reviewers. Hypothesis is disabled by default in all profiles.

## Special front matter pages {#sec-frontmatter}

### Résumé and abstract

The `resume.qmd` and `abstract.qmd` pages use CSS classes that add a left border in
HTML:

````markdown
::: {.resume-block}
Text of the résumé in French.

**Mots-clés :** mot1, mot2, mot3
:::
````

::: {.callout-important}
## French résumé mandatory for all Cnam theses

Even for a thesis written in English, a French résumé is **mandatory** according to
the {{< acrs abes >}} rules for deposit on theses.fr. This is the role of the file
`content_en/frontmatter/resume.qmd` in the English profile.
:::

### The Individual Monitoring Committee ({{< acrs csi >}})

::: {.callout-note}
## French doctoral process — the {{< acrs csi >}}

The {{< acrf csi >}} has been mandatory since 2016 for all doctoral students in
France. It meets at least once a year, independently of the thesis supervisor, to
verify progress, working conditions, and adherence to the schedule. The minutes of
the {{< acrs csi >}} meeting must be included in the defence dossier.

The HTML version of this thesis template is particularly well suited for {{< acrs csi >}}
meetings: it allows sharing a link to the online version, which is easier to navigate
than a 200-page PDF.
:::
